selectedFunctions.label: Magma Stake WMON via CoreVault
warnings: Static exact-deployment source/ABI inventory only, not a fresh RPC/storage/runtime identity, successful-transaction or financial-safety guarantee. Grants, canonical calldata/value checks, balances, allowances, pauses and independent controls remain mandatory.

Monad mainnet chain143 gMON ERC1967Proxy 0x8498312A6B3CbD158bf0c93AbdCF29E6e4F55081; MonadScan currently reports MagmaV2 implementation 0xA1f511E1442c61931ca5ace7616d2cC78497aFd2. Initial deployment implementation 0x51f392f0D6232bF695B0C7F9bb145AA51c88d8BA is NOT the reviewed active interface. Owner can upgrade and change fees, redeem delay, MEV injector and pause state.

Native depositMON/depositMONGVault spend msg.value in native MON (18-decimal wei units), not ETH. deposit/depositWMON/depositWMONGVault and mint use WMON allowance to gMON; initial proxy deployment bound WMON 0x3bd359C1119dA7DA1D913d1C4D2B7c461115433A. Nonpayable calls require zero native value. Shares are 18-decimal gMON; no caller-set minShares/maxAssets, output minimum or deadline exists.

requestRedeem/requestRedeemGVault immediately burn nonzero shares and initiate asynchronous native staking undelegation. Caller must be share owner or an already approved operator; ERC20 share allowance alone is insufficient. Nonzero controller required; only one active request per owner. Capture returned/emitted requestId; requests do not continue earning vault yield. No cancellation entry is admitted or present.

redeem(uint256,address,address) is a claim by requestId, NOT standard ERC4626 share redemption. redeem pays WMON; redeemMON pays native MON. Stored claimableTime must be reached AND underlying Monad undelegation epochs/withdrawal IDs must be ready; frontend ~12-hour wait is not a guaranteed deadline. Controller, owner, either approved operator, or protocol owner may claim to the specified receiver.

Actual withdrawn MON minus current withdrawal fee is paid; slashing, validator cash and fees can reduce output. If withdrawal is below request.assets, implementation may mint residual gMON to receiver to socialize losses; it does not simply enforce a min(request-time,current-value) payout clamp despite its source comment. withdrawalFee/rewardsFee are mutable basis points up to10000 (100%). Native-output receiver must accept empty-calldata MON transfer.

gVault variants use explicit uint64 validator IDs and fixed delegate/undelegate methods, not arbitrary target/calldata. Validator whitelist/status/pause, relative/absolute caps, minimum deposit/withdrawal, existing per-validator ownership accounting and rebalances can restrict calls. gMON transferability does not transfer gVault per-user validator allocation; transferred shares may require pooled redemption instead.

CoreVault and gVault use mutable staking dependencies and cached delegation accounting. Cache refreshes and reward-claim guards occur inside ordinary calls; current pauses, minimums, caps, fees, stake capacity and runtime eligibility were not read. No KYC/access role gate appears on reviewed ordinary Magma entry points, but interface terms exclude US persons, sanctioned jurisdictions/persons and geographic bypass; permissionless ABI access is not legal eligibility.

sourceSemantics.fixedActions: All admitted function inputs are primitive uint/address fields. Native deposits call fixed CoreVault.delegate() or gVault.delegate(receiver,valId,shares) with native assets. WMON deposits pull allowance via inherited ERC4626 then unwrap using asset(), then same fixed delegate. ReferralId is event-only data. No user target address/calldata executor, permit, callback or bridge admitted.
sourceSemantics.depositRounding: Deposit variants require nonzero calculated shares; inherited ERC4626 uses virtual+1 conversion. mint exact shares can accept zero but downstream zero native delegation may revert; source admission does not assert executable current state. No caller slippage/deadline protection.
sourceSemantics.requests: Only owner or existing operator can request; burns shares at request; nonzero controller; one active request per owner; stores owner, shares, request-time assets, claimableTime and gVault flag, then fixed undelegate. requestRedeemGVault uses exact user-validator allocation conversion rather than ordinary shared-vault rate.
sourceSemantics.claims: First uint256 of redeem is requestId despite standard ERC4626 selector. Reject nonexistent/unmatured request. Authorizes controller, owner, approved operators of either, or protocol owner. Deletes request and clears owner lock then calls fixed corresponding vault.completeUserWithdrawal(owner). Native after-fee amount paid to receiver (or wrapped/transferred WMON). Any revert rolls back state.
sourceSemantics.actualLossBehavior: Source comment describes lower-value protection, but body pays totalWithdrawnAfterFee actually returned by withdrawal dependency. _getWithdrawnShares compares totalWithdrawn to request.assets and may mint residual shares to receiver; no explicit min-payout clamp. Do not substitute generic ERC4626 redeem semantics or promise fixed requested payout.
sourceSemantics.delayFees: Stored claimableTime is request timestamp plus current redeemDelay. Later setRedeemDelay changes new requests, not existing timestamps. CoreVault/gVault precompile withdrawal readiness can delay beyond timestamp. Current withdrawalFee evaluated at settlement; current rewardsFee at reward collection. Both bounded at10000bps. Withdrawal fee rounds up; source feeReceiver transfer failure records failure and returns zero charged fee.
sourceSemantics.validatorRestrictions: Current exact gVault implementation requires whitelisted validator, not per-validator paused, cap not0, post-deposit stake within cap and minimum deposit. Exits require minimum withdraw, whitelist and sufficient user-validator tracked gMON. Per-validator allocations do not follow fungible gMON token transfers. CoreVault also requires enough eligible stake and bounded per-validator withdrawal, otherwise reverts.
sourceSemantics.cacheAndUpgrade: Ordinary methods refresh both vault caches. Owner-governed UUPS upgrade, pausing and mutable fees/delay/dependencies remain independent constraints. All standalone config/maintenance methods excluded.
sourceSemantics.eligibility: No ordinary-entry KYC/allowlist caller modifier in MagmaV2. Interface Terms section7 excludes US persons/US location and listed sanctioned territories/persons; bypass prohibited. Not a legal eligibility opinion.
sourceSemantics.notAdmitted: Direct CoreVault/gVault calls, deprecated/v1 implementation, initial implementation, validator administration, cache maintenance, operator authorization, upgrades, approvals/transfers and disabled withdraw.

Caller must be share owner or an already approved operator; ERC20 share allowance alone is insufficient. Nonzero controller required; only one active request per owner. Capture returned/emitted requestId; requests do not continue earning vault yield. No cancellation entry is admitted or present.

redeem(uint256,address,address) is a claim by requestId, NOT standard ERC4626 share redemption. redeem pays WMON; redeemMON pays native MON. Stored claimableTime must be reached AND underlying Monad undelegation epochs/withdrawal IDs must be ready; frontend ~12-hour wait is not a guaranteed deadline. Controller, owner, either approved operator, or protocol owner may claim to the specified receiver.

Actual withdrawn MON minus current withdrawal fee is paid; slashing, validator cash and fees can reduce output. If withdrawal is below request.assets, implementation may mint residual gMON to receiver to socialize losses; it does not simply enforce a min(request-time,current-value) payout clamp despite its source comment. withdrawalFee/rewardsFee are mutable basis points up to10000 (100%). Native-output receiver must accept empty-calldata MON transfer.

gVault variants use explicit uint64 validator IDs and fixed delegate/undelegate methods, not arbitrary target/calldata. Validator whitelist/status/pause, relative/absolute caps, minimum deposit/withdrawal, existing per-validator ownership accounting and rebalances can restrict calls. gMON transferability does not transfer gVault per-user validator allocation; transferred shares may require pooled redemption instead.

CoreVault and gVault use mutable staking dependencies and cached delegation accounting. Cache refreshes and reward-claim guards occur inside ordinary calls; current pauses, minimums, caps, fees, stake capacity and runtime eligibility were not read. No KYC/access role gate appears on reviewed ordinary Magma entry points, but interface terms exclude US persons, sanctioned jurisdictions/persons and geographic bypass; permissionless ABI access is not legal eligibility.
